title: Small products of D(Z)-enriched infinity categories
statement: Use complete algebroids, their object spaces and mapping objects, the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$, and fully faithful and essentially surjective maps of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and limiting cones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal V=\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ be the presentably symmetric monoidal enhanced localization of unbounded cochain complexes of abelian groups at quasi-isomorphisms of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Fix universes in which the family below is small. Let $J$ be a small set, possibly empty, and let $(\mathcal C_j)_{j\in J}$ be objects of $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$ with object spaces $X_j$. Then $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$ has a product $\prod_j\mathcal C_j$ with projections $p_j$, and: its object space is the product $\prod_jX_j$ of spaces; for objects $x=(x_j)$ and $y=(y_j)$ its mapping object is the product $\prod_j\mathcal C_j(x_j,y_j)$ in $\mathcal V$, on which $p_j$ induces the product projection; its composition and units, with all coherences, are the unique ones making every $p_j$ an enriched functor. For every $\mathcal D$ in $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$, composition with the $p_j$ gives equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(\mathcal D,\prod_j\mathcal C_j)\simeq\prod_j\operatorname{Map}(\mathcal D,\mathcal C_j)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal D,\prod_j\mathcal C_j)\simeq\prod_j\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal D,\mathcal C_j)$ of enhanced enriched functor categories as in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]; thus enriched functors, coherent enriched transformations and their higher homotopies into the product are exactly families of them into the factors. Two objects of the product are equivalent if and only if all their coordinates are. For $J$ empty the product is the one-object enriched category whose mapping object is the zero object of $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Algebroids Algd(V) as a Cartesian fibration over spaces and Cat_V as the localization of Algd(V) at the complete objects (local objects, hence closed under limits); limits of algebras over a fixed operad are computed in V. Agent statement for small products, V = D(Z).

proof.text: By [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] with R=Z, V=D(Z) is presentably symmetric monoidal, so the algebroid nodes below apply. Apply [lem-coef-algebroid-presentability] to the discrete diagram j ↦ C_j in Algd(V). Its limiting cone has object space the product of the X_j and, for x=(x_j) and y=(y_j), mapping object the limit of the C_j(x_j,y_j), namely the product in V. By the same node the compositions and units of this limit are induced by projection to every factor, so they, with their coherences, are the unique operations whose projections are the corresponding operations of the factors; equivalently, every p_j is an algebroid map. The empty diagram gives the limit with one-point object space and the empty limit as its mapping object.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived coefficient-adjunction calculation before the inverse limit; product of algebroids and mapping objects.

proof.text: Let P be the algebroid product from Step 1 and let s:E^1→E^0 be the walking-equivalence map. By [lem-coef-algebroid-completion], an algebroid is complete exactly when it is s-local, i.e. Map_Algd(E^0,A)→Map_Algd(E^1,A) is an equivalence. By the limiting-cone mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied to the product cone in Algd(V) with test objects E^0 and E^1, naturally in the test object, the map Map_Algd(s,P) is identified with the product over j of the maps Map_Algd(s,C_j). Each of these is an equivalence because C_j is complete, and by [lem-coef-kan-nerve-small-products] a product of weak homotopy equivalences of Kan complexes is one, also for J empty or infinite. Hence P is complete and lies in Cat_V.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived coefficient-adjunction calculation before the inverse limit; passage from algebroid products to complete enriched categories.

proof.text: Cat_V is a full subcategory of Algd(V) containing P and every C_j (Step 2), so for complete D the mapping spaces Map_Cat(D,P) and Map_Cat(D,C_j) are those of Algd(V); the criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] therefore shows that the projections induce Map_Cat(D,P) ≃ prod_j Map_Cat(D,C_j), naturally in D, and that (P,p_j) is a product in Cat_V. For the functor categories, [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] makes Cat_V closed symmetric monoidal with internal Hom Fun_V(D,-), the enriched category of coherent enriched functors and transformations; this is the functor category used in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. For every complete A, the adjunction gives equivalences Map_Cat(A,Fun_V(D,P)) ≃ Map_Cat(A⊗D,P) ≃ prod_j Map_Cat(A⊗D,C_j) ≃ prod_j Map_Cat(A,Fun_V(D,C_j)), natural in A, the middle one by the first paragraph with test object A⊗D; by naturality of the adjunction in the target the composite is induced by postcomposition with the p_j. By the same criterion, the maps Fun_V(D,P)→Fun_V(D,C_j) form a product cone in Cat_V, so Fun_V(D,P) ≃ prod_j Fun_V(D,C_j), the product computed by Steps 1 and 2. An equivalence of V-categories identifies objects and the mapping objects; by Step 1 the mapping objects of the product are the products of the mapping objects of the Fun_V(D,C_j), and Map_V(1,-) takes them to products of spaces ([lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]). Thus enriched functors, coherent transformations (points of Map_V(1,-) of these mapping objects) and their higher homotopies into P are exactly families of them into the C_j. An equivalence of mapping spaces alone would only see the invertible transformations; the internal-Hom adjunction is what gives the non-invertible ones.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived coefficient-adjunction calculation before the inverse limit; universal property in Cat_{D(Z)}.

proof.text: Let x=(x_j) and y=(y_j) be objects of P. By [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve] an equivalence from x to y is a point in an invertible component of Map_V(1,P(x,y)), and similarly in each C_j. Since the representable Map_V(1,-) preserves products ([lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]), Map_V(1,P(x,y)) is the product of the Map_V(1,C_j(x_j,y_j)) by the projections; for a degreewise product of Kan complexes ([lem-coef-kan-nerve-small-products]) the components are families of components. Composition and units of P are coordinatewise by Step 1, so on components composition and identities are computed in each coordinate. If f:x→y is an equivalence, each p_j(f) is one, since the algebroid map p_j preserves composition and units. Conversely, if each coordinate f_j has an inverse g_j (chosen for all j), then g=(g_j) is a point of Map_V(1,P(y,x)), and gf and fg lie in the identity components because every coordinate does. Hence a morphism of P is an equivalence if and only if every coordinate is, and choosing coordinate equivalences shows that x and y are equivalent if and only if every x_j and y_j are.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived coefficient-adjunction calculation before the inverse limit; equivalences in the product.

proof.text: Let J be empty. A cone over the empty diagram is just its apex, so a limiting cone is a terminal object; thus P has the one-point object space and its single mapping object is a terminal object of D(Z). By [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] (R=Z) every complex is fibrant and D(Z) is the localization q of this model; the zero complex is initial in complexes, hence cofibrant, and its constant cosimplicial object is a frame (all latching maps are identities of 0). By [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], Map(q0,qY) is represented by Hom(0,Y)=Δ^0 for every Y, and for cofibrant X with frame X^• the space Map(qX,q0) is represented by Hom(X^n,0)=Δ^0; since every object is equivalent to some qY and some qX with X cofibrant, q0 is both initial and terminal, so the mapping object of P is the zero object of V. Finally Step 3 gives Fun_V(D,P) ≃ the empty product, the one-object category with zero mapping object; since Map_V(1,0) is contractible, there is up to contractible choice exactly one enriched functor D→P and one coherent family of transformations, as required.
